items.title: Arthur Baron interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 3, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: They used to say that about Bush Senior but it’s more real now.

ctx.x: Well I don’t mind going to a place in our conversation where — this is not just a conversation about musicians but I’m interested in your general feeling about the state of our country.

Okay. I can tell you that it’s gotten clearer to me. The Japanese — I’ve heard that this may not be true but I heard it so long ago that it was true that I choose to believe it. And the Chinese rather. They have all these symbols for writing the language, and that the symbol for crisis is the same for opportunity, which spiritually speaking makes a lot of sense. I mean the system had gotten so corrupt, let’s face it, it’s gotten extremely corrupt on both sides of the aisle, more on one than the other, more on the…

by day, I tell myself I shouldn’t be aghast at that because we know what he’s like. I mean so there’s so much stuff, including racism now in addition to just poor leadership about the whole pandemic thing. You know standing there, “Well we’ve got ten cases, it’ll be down to five then nothing in a few days, don’t worry about it.” And then going as far as saying, “Well 100,000 is not bad, we’re doing a great job.” We’re not doing a great job, and people know it. But people also are starting to realize the only way…
